Use exact integer arithmetic and hash sets for deduplication.

source_tasks.problem: The expression $7 -  7 +  5 -  7 -  7 \cdot  5 \times  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

Consider the expression $6 \cdot  7 \cdot  7 +  2 -  6 -  3 -  8$. Fully parenthesize it in every possible way without changing the order of numbers or operations. Parenthesizations with the same numerical result count only once. How many distinct values are possible?

response.applicability: Valid for 1 to 8 integer operands in [-10,20] and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from +,-,*. Rejects malformed inputs, booleans, out-of-range operands, wrong operator counts, and unknown operators. Complexity is exponential in the worst case due to distinct value sets, but bounded by the small operand limit.
response.description: Interval dynamic programming over the fixed operand/operator sequence. For each contiguous subexpression, compute the exact set of integer values obtainable by all full parenthesizations. Combine sets across every split using the operator at that position, deduplicating with Python sets. The answer is the size of the set for the whole expression. Exact integer arithmetic avoids rounding issues. Uncertainty: assumes the intended quantity is the number of distinct numerical values over full parenthesizations preserving order, as stated in the source problems.
